Main point: Title page + Executive Summary with a "Trigger Mechanism Statistics" table summarizing historical activation stats for the Afghanistan Drought AA framework (analysis years 1984-2024).
Table "Stats by trigger":
- Window A: return period 3.2 years, activation probability 31%, years activated: 1984, 1985, 1986, 1988, 1989, 2001, 2008, 2012, 2013, 2014, 2018, 2021, 2022.
- Window B: return period 3.5 years, activation probability 29%, years activated: 1986, 1989, 2000, 2001, 2004, 2006, 2008, 2011, 2018, 2021, 2022, 2023.
Table "Overall stats":
- Overall return period: 2.3 years; Overall probability of activation: 43%.
- Average total spending per year with activation: $6.9M; Average period for total budget spend: 3.4 years; Probability of total budget spend: 29%; Average total spending per year: $2.9M.
Narrative: framework covers 4 provinces (Faryab, Sar-e-Pul, Takhar, Badakhshan); $20M combined CERF+AHF; Window A forecast trigger (1-in-4.2-yr, Feb ECMWF forecast for Mar-May rainfall); Window B observation+forecast composite indicator (1-in-5.2-yr, evaluated April).

--- page 2 ---
Main point: Narrative on modalities, learning plan, validity period, and drought context, plus a seasonal calendar chart for Afghanistan (based on FEWSNET).
Seasonal calendar chart (Jan-Dec, month-by-month bands):
- Winter wet season: Nov(part)-Feb; Spring wet season: Mar-May; Winter wet season resumes Nov-Dec.
- Spring wheat planting: Mar-Apr; Second season planting: Apr-May; Winter wheat planting: Aug-Oct.
- Poppy harvest: Apr-May; Wheat and barley harvest: May-Aug; Second season harvest (rice & maize): Sep-Oct.
- Lean season: Jan-Mar; Peak risk for spring flooding: Feb-Mar.
Key figures in text: CERF Index for Risk and Vulnerability score 74/100 (July 2024); mean annual temperature rose ~2.46°C (1951-2023); groundwater levels dropped up to 30 meters; 2023-24 precipitation deficits up to 55% below average in eastern/northeastern regions; average CERF drought allocations $13.4M (rapid response) and $11.8M (underfunded emergencies).

--- page 4 ---
Main point: Trigger threshold table (continued) and composite indicator weighting table for Window B.
Table "Triggers and thresholds":
- Window A (forecast-based): Indicator = forecasted precipitation Mar-Apr-May; Data source = ECMWF SEAS5; Evaluation = early February; Province-level return period threshold = 4.2 years.
- Window B (observation- and forecast-based): Indicator = composite drought indicator; Data source = multiple; Evaluation = early April; threshold = 5.2 years.
Table "Composite drought indicator components" (Indicator, Data Source, Value used, Weight):
- Agricultural Stress Index (ASI): FAO, end of March (Dekad 3), weight 25%.
- Vegetation Health Index (VHI): FAO, end of March (Dekad 3), weight 25%.
- Combined observed and forecasted precipitation: ECMWF (ERA5 and SEAS5), observation March / forecast Apr-May (issued April), weight 25%.
- Snow cover: ECMWF ERA5-LAND, March, weight 15%.
- Accumulated seasonal precipitation: ECMWF ERA5, total Jan-Feb-Mar, weight 5%.
- 1-metre soil moisture: ECMWF ERA5, end of March, weight 5%.
Note: return periods based on reference period 1984-2024; 4.2-yr RP = 10/41 historical years triggering per province; 5.2-yr RP = 8/41 years.

--- page 5 ---
Main point: Trigger activation protocol flowchart (steps 1-5) and a map of 31 prioritised districts across four provinces in northern/northeastern Afghanistan.
Flowchart steps: 1. Forecast is published → 2. Center for Humanitarian Data (CHD) validates forecast with Triggers sub-group (FAO), which coordinates with Ground-truthing (FAO); CHD responds within 48-72hrs → 3. CHD informs OCHA AFG, HC, AA Group, CERF, AHF (YES/NO); OCHA AFG informs ICCT and ANDMA, calls meeting to finalize geo prioritization; HC informs HCT → 4. UN & NGO partners/OCT reps receive prioritization communicated to project managers; CERF disburses funding to UN agencies, AHF authorizes spending to NGOs → 5. Delivery of assistance.
Map: Afghanistan northern/northeastern provinces (Faryab, Sar-e-Pul, Takhar, Badakhshan) highlighted in blue showing the 31 prioritised districts; inset shows location within Afghanistan (red box) relative to neighboring countries (Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, Pakistan).
District counts: Badakhshan 9 districts, Takhar 11 districts, Sar-e-Pul 5 districts, Faryab 6 districts (total 31).

Timeline chart (Jan-Jan, by month):

- Peak drought impact: gradient intensifying from ~Jun through Aug-Sep (darkest/red), fading by Oct.
- Trigger moments: "A" marked in Feb, "B" marked in Apr.
- Window A implementation: starts ~Mar, "delivery of assistance" Apr-May.
- Window B implementation: starts ~May, "delivery of assistance" Jun-Aug/Sep.

Main point: Table of CERF Funded Activities by sector, partner, funding envelope, activity, planned reach, and window.
Key rows: Cross-cutting (UNFPA/All) Early Warning messaging, Window A+B. Food Security (WFP, $2.7m): cash for food & in-kind ($59,000 people, Window A); MPCA incl. top-ups for WHH/PwD (59,000 people, Window B). Agriculture & Livelihoods (FAO, $2.6m): cash+livestock protection (1,600 HHs A / 2,000 HHs B, Window A+B); cash+seeds (1,700 HHs, Window A); cash for work/water conservation (1,617 HHs, Window A); rehabilitation of water conservation structures (11 structures, Window B). WASH (UNICEF, $3.2m): construction/rehab of water supply systems + water treatment/hygiene (29,000 people A / 36,000 people B, Window A+B); MPCA incl. top-ups (2,600 HHs, Window B). Protection: UNFPA ($1m) dignity kits (3,625+2,400), clean delivery kits (1,825), mobile health teams (53,000) all Window B; UN Women ($0.5m) safe spaces/MHPSS (780 HHs, Window B), MPCA top-up (940 HHs, Window B) and gender mainstreaming (Window A+B).

WASH $2.5m (emergency water supply, safe water storage/treatment, water conservation, hygiene kits, sanitation promotion) - Window B. Protection $0.5m (case management GBV/child/general protection, cash for protection, dignity kits, civil documentation, referrals) - Window B. Multi-Sector/MPCA $1m (single tranche MPCA aligned with CWG MEB incl. top-ups) - Window B.
Funding scenarios table: Scenario 1 - triggers reached Feb & Apr: full activity set, $10m CERF + $10m AHF. Scenario 2 - trigger only Feb: Agriculture/Food/WASH+EW, Window A CERF ($3.4m). Scenario 3 - trigger only Apr: Agriculture/Food/MPCA/Health/Nutrition/Protection/WASH+EW, Window B CERF ($6.6m) + $10m AHF.
